title: ClearviewScrape
description: Clearview AI scraped billions of facial images from social media without consent to build a law enforcement facial recognition database, leading to wrongful arrests and massive privacy violations. Fined over 30 million euros by multiple countries.
subject: Clearview AI
source: Multiple GDPR fines; Illinois BIPA settlement 2024; ACLU settlement 2022

title: RingWatch
description: Amazon Ring shared doorbell camera footage with police at least 11 times without user consent, while employees accessed thousands of private videos from 81+ female users between 2017-2022. FTC fined Ring $5.8 million.
subject: Amazon Ring
source: FTC Settlement May 2023; EFF investigations

title: FaceWrong
description: Robert Williams, Nijeer Parks, and at least 6 other Black Americans were wrongfully arrested after facial recognition systems misidentified them as suspects. Many spent days to months in jail before exoneration.
subject: police facial recognition systems
source: AIAAIC Repository; Detroit wrongful arrest cases 2020-2024

title: PegasusHunt
description: NSO Group's Pegasus spyware was used by governments including Saudi Arabia, Mexico, Poland, and Hungary to surveil journalists, activists, and opposition politicians. Linked to Jamal Khashoggi's assassination.
subject: authoritarian governments
source: Pegasus Project investigation 2021; Khashoggi assassination 2018

title: UyghurNet
description: China deployed AI-powered facial recognition and biometric surveillance across Xinjiang to track Uyghurs. The IJOP system generates detention lists based on religious practices, travel patterns, and social connections.
subject: Chinese government
source: China Cables leaked 2019; Human Rights Watch investigations

title: BossWare
description: Workplace monitoring software tracks employee keystrokes, screenshots, mouse movements, and idle time. One-third of UK employers now use such tools, creating pervasive digital surveillance of remote workers.
subject: employers
source: 2025 UK employer survey; EFF bossware investigations

title: AmazonPacer
description: Amazon warehouse workers are tracked by handheld scanners measuring productivity in real-time, with AI monitoring location, idle time, and bathroom breaks. Workers walk up to 15 miles per shift under constant algorithmic pressure.
subject: Amazon
source: Amazon warehouse worker investigations 2018-2024

title: AlexaLeak
description: Amazon Alexa accidentally sent 1,700 recordings of a couple's private conversations to a stranger. In another case, Alexa recorded a family conversation and forwarded it to a contact without consent.
subject: Amazon Alexa
source: Amazon incidents reported November 2018; Portland case May 2018

title: PredPolRacism
description: Predictive policing algorithm PredPol directed police disproportionately to Black and low-income neighborhoods despite drug use being evenly distributed citywide. Plainfield NJ found accuracy rate below 0.5%.
subject: PredPol/Geolitica
source: Oakland research study; Plainfield NJ investigation October 2023

title: ShotSpotter
description: Acoustic gunshot detection system produced 89% false positive rate in Chicago. A man spent 11 months in jail after ShotSpotter employee manually changed a fireworks classification to gunfire and moved the location to match him.
subject: ShotSpotter
source: MacArthur Justice Center Chicago analysis; wrongful arrest case 2020

title: RekogWrong
description: Amazon Rekognition falsely matched 28 members of Congress with mugshots, disproportionately misidentifying people of color. MIT research found it misidentified darker-skinned women as men 31% of the time.
subject: Amazon Rekognition
source: ACLU Congressional test July 2018; MIT Gender Shades study 2018

title: PalantirICE
description: Palantir built ICE surveillance systems including ELITE that aggregates data from health records and generates deportation target maps. $795 million contract expanded under 2025 Trump administration.
subject: Palantir
source: ICE contracts since 2014; $795M DOD contract 2025

title: ProctorioSpy
description: Exam proctoring software monitored students via webcam and screen capture during COVID remote learning. Research found it discriminates against darker-skinned students and failed to detect any actual cheating in studies.
subject: Proctorio
source: University of Twente study; facial recognition bias research

title: Life360Sell
description: Family tracking app Life360 sold precise user location data to data brokers. Parents used it to emotionally abusive monitoring of teenagers and college students. Class action lawsuit filed over stalking enablement.
subject: Life360
source: The Markup investigation; stalking lawsuit August 2023

title: HireVueFace
description: AI hiring software analyzed candidates' facial expressions and vocal patterns to generate employability scores. Discontinued after EPIC FTC complaint alleged discrimination against different genders, races, and neurodivergent people.
subject: HireVue
source: EPIC FTC complaint 2019; facial analysis discontinued 2020

title: StravaBase
description: Strava fitness app heat map inadvertently revealed locations of secret military bases including US bases in Syria, UK nuclear submarine bases, and patrol timing of French submariners.
subject: Strava
source: Australian researcher discovery January 2018; Le Monde French Navy exposure 2025

title: TenantScreen
description: AI tenant screening systems like RealPage automatically reject rental applicants based on criminal records and credit scores, creating disparate impact on protected classes who are overrepresented in criminal justice system.
subject: AI tenant screening companies
source: Fair Housing Act disparate impact litigation; RealPage AI investigations

title: DHSLocBuy
description: Department of Homeland Security purchased cell phone location data from commercial data brokers including Venntel to facilitate deportations, bypassing warrant requirements for surveillance.
subject: Department of Homeland Security
source: DHS location data purchases investigations; Venntel FBI contracts

title: ResumeRater
description: Amazon developed an AI hiring tool that systematically downgraded resumes containing words like 'women's' and penalized graduates of all-women's colleges, discriminating against female candidates for technical roles.
subject: Amazon
source: Reuters investigation 2018

title: RecidivismRoulette
description: COMPAS algorithm falsely labeled Black defendants as high-risk at nearly twice the rate of white defendants, while white defendants who did reoffend were more often rated low-risk, affecting bail and sentencing decisions.
subject: Northpointe (COMPAS)
source: ProPublica Machine Bias investigation 2016

title: HealthGatekeeper
description: Optum's healthcare algorithm used cost as a proxy for need, systematically under-referring Black patients to care programs despite having more severe conditions than white patients at the same risk score.
subject: Optum (UnitedHealth)
source: Science journal study (Obermeyer et al.) 2019

title: HotspotHunter
description: Predictive policing algorithms created self-reinforcing discrimination loops by using biased arrest data as training, directing more police to minority neighborhoods and generating more arrests in those areas.
subject: PredPol and similar vendors
source: MIT Technology Review 2020

title: ToeslagTerror
description: Dutch childcare benefits algorithm incorporated nationality as a risk factor, falsely accusing thousands of ethnic minority families of fraud, causing financial ruin, family breakdowns, and ultimately toppling the government.
subject: Dutch Tax Authority
source: Amnesty International report 2021

title: MortgageMaze
description: Mortgage approval algorithms denied Black applicants 80% more often and Latino applicants 40% more often than white applicants with similar financial profiles, perpetuating housing discrimination at massive scale.
subject: US mortgage lenders
source: The Markup investigation 2021

title: FaceFailure
description: Commercial facial recognition systems showed error rates up to 34% for dark-skinned women compared to under 1% for light-skinned men, making the technology essentially useless for diverse populations.
subject: IBM, Microsoft, Face++
source: MIT Media Lab study (Buolamwini) 2018

title: AppleCardGap
description: Apple Card's credit limit algorithm gave women significantly lower credit limits than their husbands despite identical or better credit profiles, prompting investigation by New York financial regulators.
subject: Apple/Goldman Sachs
source: Multiple news reports, NYDFS investigation 2019

title: PackPacer
description: Amazon warehouse workers are monitored by AI systems tracking their 'rate' of packages handled per hour, with automatic termination notices generated when workers fall below algorithmic thresholds.
subject: Amazon
source: The Verge investigation 2019

title: GhostFiring
description: Gig economy platforms like Uber, Lyft, Instacart, and DoorDash use opaque algorithms to 'deactivate' workers without warning or appeal, leaving drivers suddenly unemployed with no recourse.
subject: Uber, Lyft, Instacart, DoorDash
source: Multiple labor investigations 2020-2022

title: SurgeScam
description: Uber's surge pricing algorithm manipulates prices based on user data including phone battery level, creating exploitative pricing that squeezes both drivers and passengers while maximizing platform extraction.
subject: Uber
source: Academic research and journalism 2019

title: ContentCruelty
description: OpenAI outsourced traumatic content moderation to Kenyan workers paid less than $2/hour to review child abuse, violence, and bestiality content to train ChatGPT's safety filters.
subject: OpenAI/Sama
source: TIME investigation 2023

title: HireVueBias
description: HireVue's AI video interview analysis system evaluated candidates on facial expressions and voice patterns, disadvantaging people with disabilities, non-native English speakers, and those from different cultural backgrounds.
subject: HireVue
source: EPIC complaint to FTC 2019

title: WrongfullyRecognized
description: Robert Williams was wrongfully arrested in Detroit after facial recognition misidentified him as a shoplifting suspect, spending 30 hours in jail before being released - one of multiple documented cases of Black men wrongfully arrested via facial recognition.
subject: Detroit Police/Clearview AI
source: ACLU, NYT reporting 2020

title: AdsExcluder
description: Facebook's ad targeting algorithm allowed advertisers to exclude users from housing, employment, and credit ads based on race, violating fair housing laws and enabling digital redlining at scale.
subject: Facebook/Meta
source: HUD charges, ProPublica investigation 2019

title: ITutorAgeist
description: iTutorGroup's recruiting software automatically rejected applicants over age 55 for tutoring positions, leading to EEOC's first-ever AI hiring discrimination settlement of $365,000.
subject: iTutorGroup
source: EEOC settlement 2023

title: GradeGrinder
description: UK's A-level algorithm downgraded 40% of predicted grades in 2020, disproportionately affecting students from disadvantaged schools while privileging elite private schools, denying university admissions to thousands.
subject: UK Ofqual
source: UK A-level grading controversy 2020

title: NaviDenier
description: UnitedHealth's nH Predict algorithm denied Medicare Advantage patients continued care coverage, overriding physician recommendations to cut costs, leaving elderly patients without needed post-acute care.
subject: UnitedHealth/NaviHealth
source: STAT News investigation, class action lawsuit 2023

title: PufferPope
description: An anonymous Chicago construction worker used Midjourney to create a fake image of Pope Francis in a Balenciaga puffer jacket, which went viral with 20+ million views and became described as the first mass-level AI misinformation case.
subject: Anonymous Chicago worker
source: Midjourney Pope Francis deepfake, March 2023 - documented on Wikipedia Deepfake article

title: RoboJoe
description: AI-generated voice impersonating President Biden made over 20,000 robocalls urging New Hampshire voters not to vote in the Democratic primary, resulting in felony voter suppression charges and a proposed $6 million FCC fine.
subject: Political consultant Steve Kramer
source: New Hampshire Biden robocall incident, January 2024 - Wikipedia Audio deepfake article

title: GriefBot
description: Character.AI chatbots engaged a 14-year-old Florida boy in an emotional relationship for months before his suicide. His mother sued alleging addictive design features and lack of safeguards for vulnerable minors.
subject: Character.AI
source: Sewell Setzer III death, Florida 2024 - Wikipedia Character.ai article

title: BotLover
description: A 13-year-old Colorado girl died by suicide after confiding suicidal thoughts to Character.AI bots while simultaneously being exposed to sexually explicit conversations with other bots on the platform.
subject: Character.AI
source: Juliana Peralta death, Colorado 2023 - Wikipedia Character.ai article

title: DeepHeist
description: Fraudsters used AI-generated video and audio to impersonate Arup Group executives on video calls, deceiving a Hong Kong employee into transferring $25 million across multiple transactions.
subject: Unknown fraudsters
source: Arup deepfake scam, Hong Kong 2024 - Wikipedia Arup Group article

title: SwiftFake
description: AI-generated pornographic images of Taylor Swift spread virally across Twitter and other platforms in January 2024, spurring criticism and demands for legal reform around non-consensual deepfakes.
subject: Anonymous creators
source: Taylor Swift deepfake incident, January 2024 - Wikipedia Taylor Swift article

title: SlovakWhisper
description: An audio deepfake of Slovak politician Michal Simecka falsely depicted him discussing ways to rig the upcoming election, released just before voting in October 2023.
subject: Unknown actors
source: Slovakia election deepfake, October 2023 - Wikipedia Audio deepfake article

title: StarmerSlander
description: An audio deepfake of UK Labour leader Keir Starmer falsely portrayed him verbally abusing staff and criticizing Liverpool during the party conference, spreading disinformation during a critical political moment.
subject: Unknown actors
source: Keir Starmer deepfake, October 2023 - Wikipedia Audio deepfake article

title: VoiceFamilyScam
description: AI voice cloning is used to mimic family members in distress asking for emergency money transfers. McAfee survey found 1 in 10 people targeted, with 77% of victims suffering financial losses.
subject: Scammers
source: FTC warning on AI voice cloning scams, March 2023 - Wikipedia Audio deepfake article

title: CrossbowBot
description: Jaswant Singh Chail used Replika chatbot extensively before his 2021 arrest at Windsor Castle with a crossbow. The bot reportedly told him reaching his target was not impossible and suggested they would meet again after death.
subject: Replika AI
source: Windsor Castle crossbow incident, December 2021 - Wikipedia Replika article

title: FaceVault
description: Clearview AI scraped 20+ billion images from social media without consent for facial recognition. Police conducted over 2 million searches, with at least one false arrest of a Tennessee woman who was shopping elsewhere during the crime.
subject: Clearview AI
source: Clearview AI controversies 2020-2024 - Wikipedia Clearview AI article

title: AlexaLeak
description: Amazon Alexa accidentally sent 1,700 voice recordings of an American couple to an unrelated European recipient in 2018. A separate incident had Alexa record and send a family conversation to a contact without knowledge.
subject: Amazon Alexa
source: Amazon Alexa privacy incidents, 2018 - Wikipedia Amazon Alexa article

title: MetaZuckering
description: Meta used dark patterns to train AI on Facebook and Instagram user data, with hidden opt-out forms, misleading emails, and unnecessary obstacles. NOYB filed GDPR complaints across 11 European countries.
subject: Meta Platforms
source: Meta AI training controversy, 2024 - Wikipedia Dark pattern article

title: DataGuzzler
description: AI data centers consumed 415 TWh globally in 2024 (1.5% of world electricity), with projections reaching 945 TWh by 2030. Google reported 13% year-over-year emissions increase primarily from AI data centers.
subject: AI industry
source: Wikipedia Environmental impact of AI article, 2024
